why_it_matters: A compromised workload using the service account inherits full administrative privileges across project resources.
Through cloud service APIs, an attacker holding admin tokens can read, overwrite, or delete project assets and alter access policies.
Restricting service accounts to specific, non-administrative roles limits the blast radius if application credentials are leaked.
post_en:
You apply a project IAM binding with role = "roles/storage.admin".
Step 1: An attacker exploits an application vulnerability and extracts service account tokens from the instance metadata endpoint.
Step 2: Using the Google Cloud Storage API, the attacker reads, alters, and deletes storage objects across every bucket in the project.
Step 3: Through bucket IAM APIs, the attacker configures external access rules to maintain persistence without triggering project-level alarms.
CKV_GCP_42 fails when a user-managed service account is assigned any role containing admin, editor, or owner.
Fix this by changing the role argument to a least-privilege role such as "roles/storage.objectViewer".
Would your pipeline have stopped this privilege escalation before apply?
